title: National Disability Insurance Scheme Amendment (Quality and Safeguards Commission and Other Measures) Bill 2017
short_title: National Disability Insurance Scheme Amendment (Quality and Safeguards Commission and Other Measures) Bill 2017

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would create a national commission to protect people with disability from harm caused by poor-quality NDIS supports or services.

The commission would be an independent statutory body that registers and regulates providers, monitors compliance, handles complaints, and sets national standards for worker screening and behaviour support.
The bill also includes administrative changes to the NDIS Act following a 2015 independent review.
changes: Establishes an independent national commission for quality and safeguards under the NDIS.
Introduces national obligations and standards for all NDIS providers and workers, including a Code of Conduct.
Replaces the current fragmented state-based quality and safeguards system with a nationally consistent approach.
summary.affected: People with disability, their families and carers, NDIS providers and workers, and state and territory governments.

speeches.speaker: Christian Porter
speeches.brief: The National Disability Insurance Scheme Amendment (Quality and Safeguards Commission and Other Measures) Bill 2017 establishes the NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission to oversee nationally consistent quality and safety protections for the estimated 460,000 NDIS participants. The commission, costing $209 million over four years with up to 300 staff, will register providers, manage complaints and reportable incidents, reduce restrictive practices, and lead worker screening, with operations commencing in New South Wales and South Australia from July 2018.

speeches.speaker: Jenny Macklin
speeches.brief: Labor supported the bill but moved an amendment calling for a royal commission into violence and abuse against people with disability, and raised concerns about the Commonwealth minister's discretionary powers and the lack of a national workforce screening system.

speeches.speaker: Jane Prentice
speeches.brief: The bill establishes a national NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission with $209 million in funding, requiring incident reporting and a code of conduct to protect participants, and includes amendments to strengthen recognition of carers and clarify scheme definitions.

speeches.speaker: Gai Brodtmann
speeches.brief: Labor supported the NDIS amendment bill to establish an independent commission for quality and safeguards, citing specific cases of inadequate plan approvals (Elise, Wayne). The speaker also announced that a future Labor government would establish a royal commission into violence and abuse against people with disability.

speeches.speaker: Emma Husar
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the National Disability Insurance Scheme Amendment (Quality and Safeguards Commission and Other Measures) Bill but argued it only covers 10% of people with disability and called for a royal commission into violence and abuse against people with disability, citing that 90% of women with intellectual disability have been sexually assaulted and children with disability are three times more likely to experience abuse. The speaker also criticised the Turnbull government for refusing to establish such a royal commission and stated that a Shorten Labor government would do so.

speeches.speaker: Chris Hayes
speeches.brief: The member announced Labor's support for the National Disability Insurance Scheme Amendment (Quality and Safeguards Commission and Other Measures) Bill 2017, citing statistics that 90% of women with intellectual disability have experienced sexual abuse and that the NDIS covers only about 10% of people with disability. The member raised qualifications about excessive ministerial discretion, gaps in coverage for people outside the NDIS, and the lack of a national workforce screening role, while calling for a royal commission into abuse of people with disability and a Senate inquiry into the bill.

speeches.speaker: Ross Hart
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the NDIS amendment bill subject to an opposition amendment, and called for a royal commission into violence and abuse against people with disability, citing that 90% of women with intellectual disability have been sexually assaulted.

speeches.speaker: Christian Porter
speeches.brief: The NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission Bill 2017 establishes a national independent body with $209 million in funding to regulate providers, handle complaints, and oversee worker screening and behaviour support, while the government rejected calls for a royal commission and urged support for the 0.5 per cent Medicare levy increase to fully fund the NDIS.
